name: LTX 2.5 Image-to-Video — Signal Vault
wall_seconds_source: ComfyUI /history execution_start -> execution_success for the full generation (8b0ee376)
wall_seconds_note: A second queue (fd685b16) reported 10.38 s. That is NOT a generation figure — only the decode branch changed, so ComfyUI reused the cached sampler output. 70.9 s is the honest cost of this clip.

conditioning.note: production/workflows/ltx25.json is pure text-to-video. Image conditioning was added in the showcase-only copy; production was NOT modified.

prompt: A heavy armoured robot knight stands motionless at the centre of a deep underground vault, facing a tall sealed archive door. Burnished gunmetal steel plate armour with warm brushed brass trim along every bevel and rim, a rounded medieval close-helm with a deeply recessed horizontal visor slit lit by a faint cold red internal glow, a tall reinforced gorget collar, tiered pauldrons with brass edges, and a hexagonal mechanical core set into the centre of the chestplate. The vault is carved from dark stone and lined with rows of dormant metal storage racks receding into shadow. A single low amber lamp burns behind the figure, throwing a long soft shadow forward across a dusty floor; thin cold cyan light bleeds from seams in the sealed door ahead. Fine dust drifts slowly through both light sources. The camera pushes forward very slowly and steadily toward the figure from behind and slightly to the left, revealing the scale of the vault. The knight raises one gauntleted hand and rests it flat against the sealed door, and holds it there. The chest core pulses once, softly. Cinematic, high detail, restrained, solemn, film grain, shallow depth of field, warm amber against cold cyan, no camera shake.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, watermark, user interface, subtitles, captions, human face, exposed skin, extra limbs, deformed armour, chaotic motion, fast camera movement, neon signs, cyberpunk city, crowds, lens flare spam, jitter, stutter, blurry, low quality

defect_and_remedy.observed: The delivered 169-frame decode was clean through frame 160, transitional at 161, and pure noise from frame 162 to the end. Measured as high-frequency energy against a Gaussian-blurred copy: 5.17 at frame 160, 13.72 at 161, then a flat 48.6 across every frame from 162 onward.
defect_and_remedy.first_attempt: Added LTXVCropGuides between the sampler and VAEDecode, the canonical LTX guide pattern that was missing from the first build. This corrected the frame count from 177 to the requested 169 but did NOT remove the noise tail — so the extra frames and the noise had different causes.
defect_and_remedy.root_cause: 161 = 8*20+1 is itself a valid LTX grid value, and the noise begins exactly one latent frame after it. The final latent frame in the 169-frame (8*21+1) request decodes degenerately. This is a decode-side failure of the last latent group, not a conditioning or guide problem.
defect_and_remedy.remedy: Trimmed to the 161 clean frames and re-encoded at CRF 18. The final frame of the delivered file measures 5.16 high-frequency energy — in line with the body of the clip. No frames were interpolated, resampled in time, or synthesised.
defect_and_remedy.residual: Delivered duration is 6.708 s rather than 7.042 s. Within the ~7 s target.

creative_review.prompt_adherence: partial. The vault interior, dormant racks receding into shadow, amber lamp, drifting dust and cold seam light all land. The specific staged action — the knight facing a sealed door and resting a gauntlet against it — does not; the figure faces camera through most of the clip and the door beat never resolves.
creative_review.identity: strong. Guided from the anchor, the close-helm with recessed visor and red optic, tall gorget, tiered brass-rimmed pauldrons, chest core, segmented faulds and brass knee poleyns all read correctly and stay stable across the clip.
creative_review.value: the useful comparison on the page: 70.9 s here against 561.8 s for H3 R2V at the same resolution and near-identical duration. Different model class, different cost class, and LTX carries no audio.
